plan_evidence.strategy: Shrink both terms of the kernel cost model: unmasked loads/stores when BLOCK divides n, larger tiles to halve the block count, and a lower vector-op count per element
plan_evidence.code_changes: Added an unmasked contiguous kernel (_fix_nomask) selected whenever n is divisible by a power-of-two BLOCK >= 512, raised the tile cap from 4096 to 8192, replaced the 9-op floor+ceil+select+bitops truncation with a 6-op abs/floor/sign-restore form, and slimmed the host path (no memory_format on the fast path, module-level raw-stream getter, single cached entry list keyed by (dtype, n))
plan_evidence.hypothesis: The 16.7M cases are vector-instruction and per-block-overhead bound rather than DMA bound, so dropping the load/store masks, doubling the tile to 8192 elements, and cutting the truncation from 9 to 6 vector ops per element should sharply reduce device time for fix-timing-3/7/11 while leaving the 9 submit-limited cases near their host floor

expected_effect.mechanism: Removing per-element mask computation and halving the block count cuts per-block and per-element vector work at n=16.7M, where fp16 and fp32 currently cost the same ~127 us despite 2x different byte counts; the slimmer host path removes a few microseconds from the submit-limited cases
